 By Kamal Jenkins Published on November 18, 2026 Buddha Park — Reported Laos Leg Pit Stop Win
Google Street View A Poway Marine Corps captain and her mother are rewriting the record books on CBS’s long-running competition show. Riley Tejcek, 29, and her 56-year-old mom, Ann-Marie, became the first mother-daughter team to ever win a leg of The Amazing Race, and they didn’t stop there — they picked up a second first-place finish just weeks later.
 The pair’s breakthrough win came in an episode that aired October 7, when the Tejceks crossed the finish line first during the show’s Morocco leg, according to the Times of San Diego . The outlet reports that no mother-daughter duo had ever won a leg of the show before the Tejceks pulled it off. Riley called the Morocco victory monumental, saying she and her mother chose physical challenges and beat out the other teams, per the same report.
 Getting there wasn’t easy. The Times of San Diego reports that in Morocco, Riley and Ann-Marie drove for hours through the desert before tackling a grueling task that required rolling heavy tires up a hill. Ann-Marie said Riley motivated her through that tire challenge and that they finished it together, the outlet reports. Smart strategy mattered too — the station notes the Tejceks used their express pass at just the right moment in Morocco, which helped lift them into first place.
 A Second Win in Laos
 The Morocco victory wasn’t a fluke. The mother-daughter team notched a second first-place finish at Buddha Park in Vientiane, Laos, in the episode that aired November 11, according to WHNT . Over the course of the season, the Tejceks have traveled to Canada, Spain, Morocco, Albania, Sri Lanka and Laos, racing against 12 other teams for a $1 million grand prize, the Times of San Diego reports.
 Winning the Morocco leg came with its own reward. Riley and her mom were awarded a trip to Singapore, and the article notes Riley plans to use that trip for her honeymoon with her husband. CBS has scheduled another episode of the season to air Wednesday, November 18, from 9:30 to 11 p.m. ET/PT, though the eventual outcome of Season 39 remains unknown.
 From Deployment to Reality TV
 The idea for the race started far from any studio. Riley met her mother in Dubai during a 2024 deployment and told Ann-Marie then that she wanted to compete on The Amazing Race once she returned home, according to the Times of San Diego. Riley has served more than seven years as an active-duty Marine officer, and she has said her military career built the discipline, leadership skills and calm under pressure that helped on the race.
 Riley’s résumé stretches well beyond the Marine Corps. The report notes she played Division I softball at George Washington University, where GW Today confirms she earned her bachelor’s degree in 2019. She was also a Team USA bobsled pilot and won the Ms. Military pageant in 2024, per the Times of San Diego.
 Training Together, Growing Closer
 Before filming began, Riley put her mother through a training regimen built for the road ahead. She trained Ann-Marie with hikes carrying heavy backpacks, long runs on hilly roads and weightlifting sessions, the outlet reports. The two also practiced problem-solving with escape rooms and sharpened their navigation skills in an unconventional way.
 “We would literally drive somewhere on purpose and put our phones down and try to navigate without any direction,” the pair told the Times of San Diego, describing how they trained for the race’s physical, mental and navigation challenges. That preparation appears to have paid emotional dividends as well as competitive ones — Riley said she and her mother have grown much closer since the competition began, and Ann-Marie said she learned the two of them could be friends as well as mother and daughter. Riley added that she sees their run on the show as representing mothers and daughters everywhere.
 The Amazing Race, an Emmy Award-winning reality competition that pits two-person teams against each other across global locations and challenges, airs Wednesdays on CBS and streams on Paramount+.
